title: Keys cannot be mapped correctly in Chromium-based browsers

status.label: Needs current remap repro
status.detail: The report describes swapping Ctrl and Alt and losing an Alt+T browser shortcut. It includes a January diagnostic archive and browser versions, but there is no current-build reproduction or exact confirmation of whether both modifier directions are mapped.

next_action: Request the exact modifier mapping direction and a current-build comparison in Chromium and a plain text editor.

judgment.rationale: The author reports PowerToys 0.97.0, Windows build 26200, Chrome and Edge versions, and a January bug-report ZIP. The failure occurs after swapping Ctrl and Alt: pressing Ctrl (mapped to Alt)+T does not invoke the expected browser function. The issue is unassigned and has no comments; the 2026-10-11 activity only changed product labels. Current Keyboard Manager handles modifier remaps by intercepting the source virtual-key event and injecting the configured target; the report does not establish whether the swap is bidirectional, whether the same mapping fails outside Chromium, or whether the behavior persists on a current build.
evidence: The open issue is labeled Issue-Bug, Needs-Triage, and Product-Keyboard Manager; it has no assignee and no public comments.
The body lists PowerToys 0.97.0, Windows build 26200, .NET 9.0.12, Chrome 144, Edge 144, and an attached PowerToysReport ZIP.

The author says Ctrl and Alt are swapped and pressing Ctrl (mapped to Alt)+T fails to invoke the expected browser shortcut; the report does not specify whether both Ctrl-to-Alt and Alt-to-Ctrl mappings are configured.
The 2026-10-11 activity only changes product labels; no directly linked pull request was found.

At upstream main 0b1dd814878f0dfbb07787d9c3e52a2897b6f769, KeyboardEventHandlers.cpp:414-420 looks up a mapping by the received virtual-key code and :475-517 resets modifier state and injects the target key event. This source path does not by itself establish the cause of the reported browser-specific behavior.
judgment.recommended_action: Ask for the current-build mapping directions and a controlled browser versus plain-editor comparison before selecting a fix.

fix_assessment.rationale: A modifier remap defect is plausible, but current evidence does not establish the exact mapping pair, whether other applications reproduce the failure, or whether it remains on a current build.

issue_context.summary: Swapping Ctrl and Alt reportedly prevents an Alt+T shortcut from working in Chromium browsers when invoked through the remapped Ctrl key.
known_information: The report lists PowerToys 0.97.0 and a January 2026 PowerToysReport ZIP.
The author lists Windows build 26200, Chrome 144, Edge 144, and .NET 9.0.12.
The reported flow is Ctrl mapped to Alt plus T failing to invoke the expected browser function.
The issue has no comments or assignees; the 2026-10-11 timeline events only change labels.
inferences: Modifier injection or application-specific handling may be involved, but the report does not show whether an Alt-to-Ctrl reverse mapping is also configured.
A Chromium-specific shortcut interaction is possible, but the issue does not compare the same remap in a plain editor or other application.
issue_context.analysis: The January archive and application versions are already present, so do not ask for them again. The useful next evidence is the precise one-way or bidirectional mapping configuration, current-build behavior, and whether the same remapped sequence works outside Chromium. Only request a fresh /bugreport if the author confirms that the current supported build still reproduces.
initial_investigation: Read the live issue body, labels, assignees, empty comments, and timeline through 2026-10-11T16:48:54Z.
Confirmed the existing PowerToysReport ZIP and browser/Windows versions; no directly linked pull request was found.
Read current upstream source at 0b1dd814878f0dfbb07787d9c3e52a2897b6f769: src/modules/keyboardmanager/KeyboardManagerEngineLibrary/KeyboardEventHandlers.cpp:414-420 and :475-517.

information_gaps.information: Whether Ctrl-to-Alt and Alt-to-Ctrl are both configured, and the exact source/target key rows.
information_gaps.why_needed: A one-way mapping and a bidirectional swap exercise different key-event sequences and can produce different modifier state.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Share only the two relevant Keyboard Manager rows or state explicitly which directions are configured; unrelated settings are not needed.

information_gaps.information: Whether the issue persists on a current supported build and whether the same remapped Ctrl+T sequence fails in a plain text editor as well as Chrome/Edge.
information_gaps.why_needed: This separates a current Keyboard Manager modifier issue from a Chromium-specific shortcut or an already-fixed old-build behavior.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Retest the same mapping on the current build in Chrome or Edge and a plain text editor; state the exact key sequence and expected/actual result.

proposed_fixes.title: Preserve modifier state for remapped Chromium shortcuts
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: the Ctrl-to-Alt injected event or modifier-state reset may be interpreted differently by Chromium than by other applications. The report does not establish whether both directions are mapped or whether the behavior is Chromium-specific.
plan: Capture the exact one-way or bidirectional modifier mapping and reproduce on a current supported build in a browser and a plain text editor.
Trace the low-level source key and injected modifier events for the confirmed failing sequence.
If Keyboard Manager drops or misorders the modifier event, make the smallest correction and add a regression test for the confirmed mapping sequence.
verification: The confirmed remapped Alt+T sequence invokes the expected browser shortcut on the current build.
The same mapping behaves consistently in a plain text editor and the inverse Alt-to-Ctrl mapping remains correct when configured.

confidence.rationale: The report gives a concrete shortcut and existing diagnostics, but the mapping direction, cross-application behavior, and current-build status remain unknown.

actions.label: Approve current modifier remap investigation
actions.note: Proceed with a code design only if the current-build browser/editor comparison confirms a Keyboard Manager defect.

actions.label: Request modifier directions and current repro

comment.body:
The report already includes the January diagnostic ZIP and browser/Windows versions. To distinguish a modifier-remap issue from a Chromium-specific shortcut, could you share:
- Whether the mapping is Ctrl-to-Alt only or also Alt-to-Ctrl, and the exact relevant mapping rows.
- Whether the same sequence still fails on a current PowerToys build in Chrome/Edge and in a plain text editor, with the physical keys pressed and expected/actual result.
If it still reproduces on the current build, a fresh /bugreport immediately after the failure would help; there is no need to re-upload the January archive.
